Mivtzoim—they feel like they’ve been around forever! Can you even imagine life without them? Yet, unbelievably, before the Rebbe introduced each of the mitzvah campaigns

that we know so well, they simply didn’t exist. Join us as we explore imaginary old diaries that

could have belonged to kids just like you— kids who might have lived during the time when the Rebbe first announced many of these mivtzoim.

When you were born, did your parents buy you a letter in the Children’s Sefer Torah? Levi’s parents didn’t sign him up until he turned 10, but it’s not because they forgot when he was a baby! Open up Levi’s diary to discover what it was like when Mivtza Ois b’Sefer Torah began. Ois B’Sefer

I actually finished cleaning my room just in time for bedikas chametz! I’m joking, that’s not the exciting news. There was another surprise farbrengen tonight! Three nights of farbrengens in a row!

The Rebbe instructed to continue writing the Torah tomorrow (Erev Shabbos), so we have a chazaka of writing the Torah on three consecutive days, before pausing for Pesach.

ר"ח אייר Dear Diary, I need to give you a major update on Mivtza Ois b’Sefer Torah! There are now official sign-up forms, and … drumroll please … I have my own letter! And a certificate! My letter is in Parshas Lech Lecha. I’m so curious which letter it is, and whose letters are next to mine, but the Rebbe said not to include those details. We don’t want kids feeling bad if their letter is in a less- happy section. When the forms were

given out, my parents sat us all around the table with pencils and erasers, so we could fill out the forms by ourselves. The Rebbe said that when a child writes “he sticks his tongue out between his teeth, deliberates to himself, and rolls up his sleeves. Then, he looks at his pen or pencil and thinks about how to turn it, and works hard to make sure that the shape of the letters comes out right…” That’s literally what Berel and Devoirie were doing! The Rebbe said when kinderlach work so hard

to do something special, it brings strong love from Hashem! Baby Yehuda can’t write, but Mommy made sure he was watching when she filled out his form. Our certificates are all hanging in the dining room so people who visit will want to buy a letter for their kids, too! The certificates are beautiful, exactly how the Rebbe instructed them to be, with pictures of heilige places in Eretz Yisroel. But get this—at tonight’s farbrengen, the Rebbe said we need to complete the Torah by Erev Rosh

Hashana! That’s just five months away! Here’s the math: There are 304,805 letters in the Torah. I’m not sure how many of us have already bought letters, but even if we total 50,000 (high estimate!), we still need to sign up almost 13,000 kids every week!! There’s a massive campaign all over the world to sign kids up! Cars with loudspeakers, ads, booths in the center of town … I wonder what else will be done to meet our goal! Levi

I don’t know what’s going on, but something definitely is. The Rebbe sent out a michtav klali yesterday, saying that the Yidden’s gashmiyus and ruchniyus well- being are in danger, and we need to unite with Ahavas Yisroel. The Rebbe later said that it's especially important to sign kids up for the Children's Sefer Torah between Lag BaOmer and Shavuos.

It’s the nuclear bombs that are being built! That’s the danger! The Rebbe explained at the Shabbos farbrengen last week that it only takes one meshugane person to press a button and destroy the entire world!

The first step to avert the danger is to have Ahavas Chinam for one another. But that’s not enough—we need a mitzvah to bring us all together. This mitzvah is the Children’s Sefer Torah!

The Rebbe pushed us even more to sign kids up for the Torah, saying that we must report to the Rebbe how

Mazel Tov! The Children’s Torah has been completed! (I know I told you that the deadline was Erev Rosh Hashana, but the Rebbe brought it earlier, to Yud-Beis Tammuz, and then to Chof Menachem Av.)

My father heard all about the incredible siyum in Eretz Yisroel. The Torah was finished in the Tzemach Tzedek shul (in Yerushalayim), and everyone paraded to the Kosel with fiery torches and a marching band, where thousands of people and other Sifrei Torah greeted the new Children's Torah.

Afterwards, the Torah was brought back to the shul for a se’uda and farbrengen late into the night.

Something tells me that this won’t be the last Children's Torah to be written…

Dear Diary, Ah, finally home from school so I can write about the Rebbe’s birthday farbrengen last night! Remember how a few months ago, the Rebbe started Tzivos Hashem, the army that unites all Jewish children? The Rebbe said that sometimes it’s hard for the soldiers to feel this achdus, which is why we have things like a matching uniform and a logo… But of course, the Rebbe continued, real achdus comes from Torah! The Rebbe suggested a totally new mivtza: Writing a Sefer Torah just for kids under Bar & Bas Mitzvah,

with every child buying their own letter for $1. This is how we can show that all kids are united through Torah! The Rebbe instructed that the Torah be written in Yerushalayim very quickly, and in the best way possible. Wanna hear something wild? In New York, the farbrengen finished at 12:30 am, but in Eretz Yisroel, it was 6:30 am. Since it was already daytime, they immediately got started planning, and within a few hours, the Torah was underway! I can’t wait to buy my own letter! Levi P.S. Whew—I’m writing this just a few hours after what I wrote above, but that was

right after school (when I was supposed to be Pesach cleaning under my bed). When I finally got under there and felt something suspiciously gooey and wiggly, I was suddenly shlepped out by a voice calling me. “Levi quick! A surprise farbrengen!” Tatty urged. We ran to 770, where the Rebbe announced that the first line of the Children’s Sefer Torah has been written! Do you get it?! The mivtza was only announced last night! The Rebbe then described more about the mivtza: how each kid gets a letter, how the certificates should look, and other details. This is getting so real, so fast!
